significance: A shore shrine near Fudam village on Diu where five Shiva lingas of different sizes are carved among rocks at the tide line, submerged at high tide and exposed at low. The name is read as Ganga plus Ishwar, for Shiva who received the descending Ganga in his hair.
story: The five lingas are said to have been carved and worshipped by the Pandavas while they were living in disguise during their exile.
